sub1: Clean Final Tuned with a tenth Sunday shift added and the wheel reordered — fatigue factors 3 → 2, longest run 9 → 6, and Sunday's fit down by a further fifth
sub7: Why the Sunday shift could not simply be written in, what the reorder is, and the two other answers that were measured
method:
1 · The cell. The ask was a tenth Sunday duty that fits December better. Every placement was measured — every line with a Sunday rest day, every start on the five-minute grid, four lengths, 1,771 placements clearing a 12h30 rest — and the demand curve is unambiguous: an evening turn, 15:25–23:25, takes Sunday's misfit from 44.9 to 35.3. But on the parent's line order that turn trips a factor wherever it goes: a worked Sunday joins the week before to the week after, so either FF11 (more than 13 shifts without a 48-hour break) or the 55-hour week appears. Only two lines could take any Sunday duty without a new factor, and both of them made the fit worse.

2 · The reorder. So the wheel was reordered — whole weeks only (optimise.mjs, LINES_ONLY=1), which is the smallest edit that can move a fatigue factor, because the factors are properties of which week follows which. Every week pattern is intact; 16 of the 20 working weeks change line number and 7 lines stay where they were; the week that gains the Sunday cell is the parent's week 24, now at line 5. Result: factors present 3 → 2, longest run 9 → 6, full weekends off 4 → 5, the worst seven-day window 51.6h → 50.9h, tightest rest 12h30. Coverage, headcounts and the contract are invariant by construction, and the script asserts all three. It reproduces exactly from the committed start grid with the reorder search at seed 7 — the command is in the proposals README, beside the two other answers below.

3 · The two other answers, both in the table opposite. Four swaps only is the smallest reorder that reaches two factors: 17 lines untouched, but the run stays at 8, weekends fall to 3 and the 55-hour window sits at 54.7 — eighteen minutes from the line. Full re-search lets duties move between weeks as well: one factor, six weekends, 13 of 20 weeks a single turn — and 19 of the 20 working weeks rewritten. This proposal is the middle of those three; which end the room prefers is the room's call, not the search's. Not a recommendation.

sub3: What the added Sunday buys, what the reorder buys, and the weekday column neither of them touches
coverNote: four weeks at lines 1, 7, 12 and 17 — gaps of 8, 6, 5, 5, exactly as the parent has them: the reorder holds the cover weeks fixed and swaps only working weeks
intro2:
This is “Clean Final Tuned” with one cell added — a tenth Sunday duty, 15:25–23:25 — and the wheel then reordered, whole weeks only, so that the added Sunday does not lengthen anybody's run. Ten on a Sunday is the December headcount, met for the first time in this family.

Measured against the December curve the way every proposal here is measured — the squared gap between each hour's share of demand and its share of cover, lower being better — Sunday falls from 44.9 to 35.3; Saturday stays at 20.5 and the five weekdays at Mon 28.4 · Tue 43.6 · Wed 42.3 · Thu 48.8 · Fri 31.0, because no weekday or Saturday cell was touched. Fatigue factors present go from three to two, the longest worked run from nine days to six, and full weekends off from four to five. The Wk fit column opposite is the fit of the average weekday, so it reads the same for this design, its parent and its grandparent — no weekday cell moved between them; page 4 carries each day's own figure.
dutyNote: Why the duties land where they do: Monday to Saturday still totals exactly 42,000 minutes — 20 × 35h to the minute — with the parent's daily split untouched: Mon 6,225 · Tue 7,205 · Wed 7,205 · Thu 7,780 · Fri 7,690 · Sat 5,895. Sunday rises from 4,635 to 5,115 minutes, ten duties where there were nine, and it sits on top of the contract as rest-day working, as every Sunday here does. The reorder moved no duty between days — each day's multiset of turns is exactly the parent's plus the one Sunday cell, asserted by the search rather than argued — so the coverage rows opposite differ from the parent's on Sunday alone.
openQuestionsHeading: Five things to settle before it is frozen
openQuestions: Sunday now closes with five, where the shape asks three. The parent already closed with four; the added turn finishes at 23:25 because 22:00 was Sunday's deepest remaining shortfall and the curve asked for exactly that. A 15:20–23:20 turn keeps the closers at four and costs 0.6 of fit — if the rule wins, that is the change. Sixteen line numbers move. Every week is intact, but a person's line number is what they know, and 16 of the 20 working weeks change theirs. The Four swaps only row opposite is the small version and it shows what small costs: run 8, three weekends, and a 55-hour window eighteen minutes from breaching. The week that gains the Sunday. The parent's week 24 — now line 5 — works Sunday 15:25–23:25, Monday off, then three earlies from Tuesday: a late into an early across one rest day. Legal by a wide margin (30h55) and a five-day week where it was four; it is the one week here whose shape a member would notice changing. FF15 sits exactly on its threshold. The longest run of early shifts is 4, and the factor reads “more than 4” — clear, not comfortably. Everything the parent did not answer, it still does not. Saturday opens with five and closes with three against four and four; Saturday carries 12 against 14; 4.35 days a week against 4.2; the longest late is 8h40 against a longest early of 8h30; Thursday is still the worst-fitting day at 48.8; two factors — a block of early starts with no rest after it, and start times that move more than two hours inside a block — remain present, and the Full re-search row shows what clearing one of them costs.
